name: Business Model Analysis for UX
description: Understanding the business context in which UX design operates. Covers both analysis of existing business models (Business Model Canvas, Lean Canvas) and evaluation of competitive and strategic landscape for new ventures (Inspirator, Competitor Analysis, Porter's Five Forces, SWOT). UX designers who understand business model fundamentals make design decisions that are commercially viable, not just user-desirable.

subskills.name: Business Model Canvas (BMC)
subskills.description: Osterwalder's 9-block framework for mapping an existing business: Customer Segments, Value Propositions, Channels, Customer Relationships, Revenue Streams, Key Resources, Key Activities, Key Partnerships, and Cost Structure. UX designers use BMC to understand which user segments generate value, what the core proposition is, and how customer relationships shape interaction design.

subskills.name: Lean Canvas
subskills.description: Ash Maurya's startup-focused adaptation of the BMC, replacing partner/activity/resource blocks with Problem, Solution, Key Metrics, and Unfair Advantage. Suited for early-stage product discovery. UX designers use it to align design sprints with validated problem-solution fit hypotheses.

subskills.name: Inspirator Analysis
subskills.description: Identifying non-competing products or services that excel at the behavioral mechanics the new product aims to achieve. Inspirators are studied for their engagement patterns, habit loops, and UX innovations that could be adapted. Differs from competitor analysis in that inspirators may come from entirely different industries.

subskills.name: Competitor Analysis
subskills.description: Systematic evaluation of direct competitors' UX, features, pricing, positioning, strengths, and weaknesses. Covers feature matrix comparisons, UX teardowns (heuristic evaluation of competitor interfaces), and identifying market gaps that represent UX opportunities.

subskills.name: Porter's Five Forces
subskills.description: Strategic framework analyzing industry competitiveness across five dimensions: competitive rivalry, supplier power, buyer power, threat of new entrants, and threat of substitutes. Informs UX decisions about product stickiness, switching cost design, and where to invest in differentiation.

subskills.name: SWOT Analysis
subskills.description: Strengths-Weaknesses-Opportunities-Threats framework applied to product or organization context. UX teams use SWOT to identify internal design capabilities and external market opportunities that shape the product strategy and interaction design priorities.

junior.description: Reads and interprets a Business Model Canvas and can conduct structured competitor UX teardowns.

mid.description: Uses Lean Canvas for problem-solution fit discovery, finds cross-industry behavioral inspirators, and synthesizes SWOT insights into design priorities.

senior.description: Applies Five Forces analysis to identify competitive moats, switching cost opportunities, and product differentiation vectors that guide long-term UX strategy.
